region: Barsotti Vineyard · El Dorado County, California
about: Jolie-Laide is French for “pretty-ugly”, finding beauty in the unexpected, and it sums up Scott and Jenny Schultz’s project. Scott came up through restaurants, serving as a sommelier at Thomas Keller’s Bouchon, then worked the cellar at Realm and became assistant winemaker to Pax Mahle at Wind Gap. He launched Jolie-Laide in 2010 with about 100 cases of Trousseau Gris. Jenny, a winemaker in her own right, now shares the work, and each vintage gets a new label painted by a Bay Area artist.

The fruit comes from Barsotti Vineyard, high in the Sierra Foothills of El Dorado County at nearly 3,000 feet, where decomposed pink granite, organic farming and cool nights let the grapes ripen slowly and hold their acidity. The 2024 rosé is 70% Gamay and 30% Cabernet Franc, pressed as whole clusters and aged in neutral oak puncheons. Jolie-Laide picks about a month earlier than most California producers, uses native yeasts, and adds little or no sulphur until bottling. The result is a light, dry, mountain-grown rosé of about 12.5% alcohol, built for freshness rather than sweetness.
